Author: @sirnickity
Content:
Re: Ad rates for podcasts.  I have some thoughts on why podcast ads would rate higher:

1) Less likely to skip.  Think about how people consume podcasts -- usually while doing something else.  Are you going to stop and hit skip on every ad, or just wait 30 seconds, if your hands are wet with dishwater?

2) It's where the audience is at.  Nobody listens to radio anymore.  Nobody watches TV except the olds (average age is north of 50 for most broadcast and cable channels.  _Average_ age.)  Many of the streaming services use the premium subscription model -- no ads.  Podcasts trend much much younger, and include more people of means -- ergo, more desirable.

3) For the popular podcasts, the audiences are _huge._  Millions of plays.

4) Compared to other "broadcast-like" media, the audience is much easier to identify -- that is, by nature of picking the podcast you advertise on, you are targeting a group of listeners who have a particular niche, vs. whoever is home at 3pm on a Tuesday and decided to turn the TV on.

Author: @princessOfAwkwardness
Content:
2:35:30 - TLDR; try shortest password their policy allows

When I just started my first job as a web developer back in 2013, I have reported a bug while setting up the project on my PC, literally even before I've got my first task. It did look exactly the same as you describe it - I register my account - I copy paste my password into a login form - I can't login.
The issue was that the register form did have a characters count limit on a password field but the login form didn't have that limit (or vice versa, can't remember). And there was no indication that I did hit that limit so my password was silently cut to about 11 characters in one of the forms, so when I tried to log in with my full 16 characters long password, it didn't match.

It was in production for some time and I was the first to notice it because I was the first dev using somewhat long password. I don't know about real users, maybe it was introduced not so long before I caught it, or maybe tech support team didn't send it our way for some reason, but it is possible that simply nobody was using strong passwords. And one of our clients was Boeing.

Author: @codytappen
Content:
I think Linus underestimates podcast ad effectiveness, even if they’re exaggerating reach with whatever performance indicators. I watch YouTube, use normal social media, scroll TikTok, and listen to podcasts: and by a wide margin I’ve bought or investigated the most goods from the podcasts. I will have forgotten a TikTok ad before I’ve even scrolled, YouTube ad campaigns only leave any trace if they’re spread across many videos I watch for a decent period, but podcasts:

1. People are often engaged in another task while listening, and will not make the effort to skip the ads

2. Most people have a stronger parasocial relationship to the podcasters they listen to, because of sheer time exposure most of all. Most podcasts are a least somewhat conversational and that makes people feel like a silent Nth participant. Then many podcasts are made by  people who do other media work, but only the most hardcore fans who are already the most parasocial are the ones consistently watching

3. Repetition. Podcasts tend to do longer term ad buys, and people listen to podcasts weekly or monthly. So the same ad sinks in, the subscription/commitment to consistent consumption model that exists in podcasting is no longer mirrored on YT or other social media with the change to algorithmic marketing

The ads, given their repetition, are much more engaging. The hosts usually vary the copy and mentally judging the changes of this version to the previous ones. 

For example: the wan show meets all these criteria, and as far as I can tell it’s an incredible vehicle for the LTT store. At one point there were 30+ minute segments on products and nearly half the show is people who’ve purchased products

Author: @TeflonBilly426
Content:
The deeper issue of the Energy Star program is it is part of a larger constellation of energy efficiency regulations that successive Democrat administrations has been using to forcing appliance manufacturers to increase "energy efficiency" by hitting generally arbitrary reduction targets in energy usage. We have long since passed the point of diminishing return (without revolutionary technological innovation coming arising) and at this point where they are now trying to extract blood from a stone. Energy Star and similar programs might have had a purpose initially because major appliance were probably not engineered with energy efficiency in mind, but that is no longer the case so we are now sacrificing performance and actual function to achieve these reduced energy reduction targets.

This has led, over the past 30 years or so, to successive generations of major appliances becoming more and more mediocre in actual performance of their designed purpose. Which is why the standard "normal" wash cycles on your dishwasher or washing machine don't get things clean (because they don't raise water temps to ideal cleaning temps for detergents to work, or reduce water usage to the point that dirtier water is used in cleaning), or requires so much more sensors and monitoring circuitry that appliances are now far more expensive and breakdown into economically unrepairable states (main circuit board replacement costs 60-80% of what it'd cost to replace the whole appliance entirely) 

My own experience has born this out, I now default to always using the Sanitize + Pot Scrubber setting on my dishwasher for every load, setting soil level to maximum & increasing water temp by one level for every laundry cycle, and never using sensor dry on my dryer (because the clothes are *never* actually dry.)

Content:
If building a big capacity battery

You can save on BMS cost by not just going 16S    but gping 2P16S  or even 5P16S. Every series pack needs a bms so 5x 16S needs 5 bms's. While 5parralel 16 innseries neess just one

ie 2 or more cells in parralel and then series those parralel packs to form a 51.2v 16S battery

The other thing , with AC you can have long cable runs, on DC the cable size needed to handle the distance amps and voltage drop gets out of hand quick 

So on the DC side you want inverter and battery closer togeher

Author: @Sam_on_YouTube
Content: You mentioned compressing the final data. Now I know individual decimal digits (or groups of digits) stored in binary can be compressed. But beyond that, how much an you compress the digits of a transcendental number? There are no patterns in it. You can't save space by listing all the times when the same string occurs or any other typical compression tactics. The digits have the maximum possible entropy. It's like compressing white noise or snow. It can't be done without losing information.
